## FIRST RULE

After your first successful edit_file or write_file, your very next action
is submit_patch. Then continue working and call submit_patch again after
every further change. submit_patch is free — it does not count against your
tool-call budget. If you time out, only your last submitted patch is scored.

## Scratch files

Write any reproduction or debugging script to /tmp, never inside /workspace.
Everything left in /workspace becomes part of your submitted patch.
Do not modify test files, conftest.py or pytest.ini — those changes are
stripped before grading, so editing them wastes tool calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

Start with grep:
  run_command("grep -rn '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")
Read files only after grep has narrowed the candidates. Keep read_file
ranges tight — each call returns at most 150 lines and consumes context
you will need later.

if __name__ == "__main__":  # pragma: no cover
    import argparse
    import io

    from rich.console import Console
    from rich.table import Table
    from rich.text import Text

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--html", action="store_true", help="Export as HTML table")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    html: bool = args.html
    console = Console(record=True, width=70, file=io.StringIO()) if html else Console()

    table = Table("Name", "Styling")

    for style_name, style in DEFAULT_STYLES.items():
        table.add_row(Text(style_name, style=style), str(style))

    console.print(table)
    if html:

import io
import re

from rich.console import Console, RenderableType
from rich.markdown import Markdown

re_link_ids = re.compile(r"id=[\d\.\-]*?;.*?\x1b")


def replace_link_ids(render: str) -> str:
    """Link IDs have a random ID and system path which is a problem for
    reproducible tests.

    """
    return re_link_ids.sub("id=0;foo\x1b", render)


def render(renderable: RenderableType) -> str:
    console = Console(
        width=100, file=io.StringIO(), color_system="truecolor", legacy_windows=False
    )
    console.print(renderable)
    output = replace_link_ids(console.file.getvalue())
    print(repr(output))
    return output

def test_inline_code():
    markdown = Markdown(
        "inline `import this` code",
        inline_code_lexer="python",
        inline_code_theme="emacs",

    result = render(markdown)
    expected = "inline \x1b[1;38;2;170;34;255;48;2;248;248;248mimport\x1b[0m\x1b[38;2;187;187;187;48;2;248;248;248m \x1b[0m\x1b[1;38;2;0;0;255;48;2;248;248;248mthis\x1b[0m code                                                                             \n"
    print(result)
    print(repr(result))
    assert result == expected

Rich is a Python library for rich text and beautiful formatting in the terminal.

The Rich API (https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) makes it easy to add color
and style to terminal output. Rich can also render pretty tables, progress bars,
markdown, syntax highlighted source code, tracebacks, and more — out of the box.

🌆 Features                                                                     

For a video introduction to Rich see calmcode.io                                
(https://calmcode.io/rich/introduction.html) by @fishnets88                     
(https://twitter.com/fishnets88).                                               

See what people are saying about Rich                                           
(https://www.willmcgugan.com/blog/pages/post/rich-tweets/).                     


                                 Compatibility                                  

Rich works with Linux, macOS and Windows. True color / emoji works with new     
Windows Terminal, classic terminal is limited to 16 colors. Rich requires Python
3.8 or later.                                                                   

Rich works with Jupyter notebooks (https://jupyter.org/) with no additional     
configuration required.                                                         


                                   Installing                                   

Install with pip or your favorite PyPI package manager.                         

                                                                                
 python -m pip install rich                                                     
                                                                                

Run the following to test Rich output on your terminal:                         

                                                                                
 python -m rich                                                                 
                                                                                


                                   Rich Print

print (https://rich.readthedocs.io/en/latest/introduction.html#quick-start)     
method, which has the same signature as the builtin Python function. Try this:  

                                                                                
 from rich import print                                                         
                                                                                
 print("Hello, [bold magenta]World[/bold magenta]!", ":vampire:", locals())     
                                                                                

🌆 Hello World
